newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ka Wah cuts HK mortgage rates by 0.25 pt.
newsitem.headline: Ka Wah cuts HK mortgage rates by 0.25 pt.

text.p: Ka Wah Bank Ltd said it cut local residential mortgage rates by 0.25 percentage point on Monday to prime plus 0.25 percentage point for civil servants and professionals and plus 0.5 percentage point for others.
Vice president Norman Lok said the rates had previously been prime plus 0.5 point for civil servants and professionals and plus 0.75 point for others.

Hong Kong's standard mortgage rate is 1.75 percentage points above prime rate, which currently stands at 8.5 percent. But many banks in the territory have cut mortage rates to prime plus 0.5-1.0 point.
Ka Wah's new scheme also entitled the borrower to a 50 percent discount from first-year fire insurance premium, and had abolished the previous handling charge of HK$2,000 each deal, Lok said.
The bank also extended the maximum duration of loan. The sum of the loan period and the property's age should not exceed 40 years now, versus the previous 30 years.
Ka Wah Bank is a unit of Beijing-based China International Trust and Investment Corp.
